item.title: Japan launches historic mission to collect samples from Mars moon Phobos
item.description: Japan's MMX mission will collect at least 10 grams of material from Phobos and return it to Earth by 2031, aiming to resolve how Mars' two moons formed and evolved ...
item.dc:creator: Unis Ahmad Dar
item.content:encoded: Japan has launched a $578 million mission to bring back the first samples from a Martian moon, Reuters reported, in a bid to settle how Phobos and Deimos formed. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft aboard its H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Centre on October 20. The spacecraft is expected to reach the Martian system in August 2027 and return samples to Earth in 2031. The mission aims to collect at least 10 grams of material from Phobos, the larger and closer of Mars’ two moons. If successful, it will become the first mission to return samples from a Martian moon, giving scientists material they can examine in laboratories on Earth. Why Phobos? Phobos offers scientists a way to investigate the Martian system without attempting the more difficult task of collecting and returning samples directly from Mars. The moon measures roughly 27 km by 22 km by 18 km and orbits about 6,000 km above Mars. Its relatively weak gravity makes landing and collecting material technically different from operating on a planet with stronger gravity. Its proximity to Mars is another advantage. Scientists believe Phobos may have accumulated debris ejected from the planet by meteorite impacts. Studying this material could provide evidence of how Mars evolved over billions of years. Phobos may also preserve clues about the composition and history of small bodies in the Solar System. Determining whether it originated from a collision involving Mars or was captured from elsewhere would help researchers understand how planetary systems formed. Beyond planetary science, MMX will test technologies needed for future missions to Mars, including surface landings, sample collection and the return of material across interplanetary distances. What will the probe do? MMX will travel for about a year before reaching the Martian system in August 2027. It will then conduct detailed observations of Phobos and study Deimos during flybys. A French-German rover, named IDEFIX, will be deployed to Phobos to examine its surface and help assess suitable landing sites. The main spacecraft is expected to land on Phobos around 2029-30 and collect samples using its sampling equipment. JAXA aims to retrieve at least 10 grams of surface material. The spacecraft will then leave the Martian system and begin its return journey, with the sample capsule expected to reach Earth in 2031. The mission is designed to last about five years. Japan has earlier sent two missions to return samples from asteroids–Hayabusa and Hayabusa2. However, travelling to the Martian system, operating in Phobos’ low-gravity environment and returning samples to Earth will pose a different challenge, scientists say.

item.title: Infantino set to visit Japan to seek Asian backing for FIFA re-election bid
item.description: The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Sports / Football News / Infantino set to visit Japan to seek Asian backing for FIFA re-election bid

Infantino set to visit Japan to seek Asian backing for FIFA re-election bid The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded

Gianni Infantino, president of FIFA | Image: Bloomberg

AP Tokyo 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 20 2026 | 4:01 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Gianni Infantino's campaign for re-election as FIFA president is set to move this week to Japan and a meeting scheduled for Wednesday with the Asian Football Confederation. This comes after Infantino apologized last week in Zurich, Switzerland, to FIFA's 37-member ruling council - which he chairs - for "mistakes" he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2 billion sell-off plan for the World Cup. The council is the main decision-making body at FIFA with a global spread of officials. The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded. Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the president of the AFC, expressed early opposition to Infantino and his plan to create a subsidiary to run the World Cup, but may have moved closer to Infantino, The Athletic has reported.

Also Read

FIFA chief Infantino apologises for World Cup row, fails to appease critics

FIFA plans to double development funding; India could receive $25 million

UEFA sets criteria for candidate to challenge Infantino and overhaul FIFA

FIFA leadership battle looms as European football chiefs discuss Infantino

Saudi Arabia shelves $2.5 billion Neom Stadium plan for 2034 World Cup

Infantino has offered to critics an open, independent review of how FIFA makes its decisions. Infantino is electioneering   An Associated Press tally indicates Infantino is close to landing the simple majority of the 211 FIFA member federations he needs to win re-election in March to a fourth term. Some of the deciding votes could some from Asia. The AFC had joined the criticism of Infantino in the wake of the proposed World Cup sell-off, but its members appear far from united. Qatar, the 2022 World Cup host, has expressed support for the FIFA leader while Jordan has declared its opposition. The FIFA Council is scheduled to meet next on Dec. 16 in Doha, Qatar.

The Associated Press count shows 87 of the 211 FIFA Member federations have indicated support for Infantino either in individual comments or by endorsing statements of support by their regional confederations. The largest block of opposition comes from Europe. The FIFA voting system   No sitting FIFA president has lost an election since 1974. The deadline for a candidate to file against Infantino is Nov. 18. FIFA rules state candidates must have "played an active role in association football (e.g. as a player or an official within FIFA, a confederation or an association, etc.) for two of the last five years before being proposed." They must have "declarations of support" from at least five of the 211 members. "FIFA is a massive patronage network," Jules Boykoff, a political scientist at Pacific University and a former professional soccer player, told The Associated Press. "It brings in billions from the men's World Cup and distributes it to football associations around the world in exchange for loyalty."   "The funds that FIFA distributes to soccer bodies around the world are meant to develop soccer, but there's scant oversight," Boykoff added. "To say FIFA is in need of structural overhaul it to make an enormous understatement.

item.title: PNB cautions customers of AI-led cyberattacks amid cyber fraud surge
item.description: bank informed customers that fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated methods to make their attempts more convincing ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Banking / PNB cautions customers of AI-led cyberattacks amid cyber fraud surge

PNB cautions customers of AI-led cyberattacks amid cyber fraud surge Bank informed customers that fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated methods to make their attempts more convincing

| Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 20 2026 | 4:00 PM IST

Listen to This Article

State-run Punjab National Bank (PNB) has cautioned its customers about AI-enabled cyberattacks, especially AI voice cloning, deepfakes, and phishing, amid surging incidents of fraud, and has advised them to remain vigilant. Highlighting that October is observed as National Cyber Security Awareness Month every year, the bank informed customers that fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated methods to make their attempts more convincing. "Many cyber frauds today exploit human behaviour, particularly trust, fear, urgency and everyday digital habits. Fraudsters may imitate the voice or appearance of your family members, friends, or trusted persons and create a false emergency to seek an urgent transfer of money," PNB MD and CEO Ashok Chandra said in his message to customers.   Similarly, fraudulent emails, SMS or messages may appear highly personalised and like genuine bank communications, making them more difficult to identify, he said, adding that they create panic and make customers act without verification. In view of rising incidents of cybercrimes across the country, the domestic public and private sector banks are actively ramping up IT and cybersecurity investments to combat evolving threats from advanced artificial intelligence, quantum computing risks, and strict regulatory mandates from the Reserve Bank of India. Also Read

Nifty PSU Bank index surges 3%; PNB, PSB, Canara, Union Bank soar up to 8%

PNB's foreign bank MoU 10-15 days away, says MD & CEO Ashok Chandra premium

Punjab National Bank Q2 results: Net profit rises 13% to ₹5,532 crore

PM Modi calls for global framework to tackle cyber fraud, deepfakes

Axis, AU Bank, PNB: Brokerages identify 5 bank stocks after RBI hikes rate

Pointing out that all these scams run on the fuel called urgency, 63SATS Cybertech Joint MD & Joint CEO Srinivas L said, "A cloned voice of a son saying he has been arrested. A video of a police officer threatening a digital arrest. A message saying the bank account will be blocked in an hour. The technology has changed, but the playbook has not. It makes people panic, which pressurises them to pay."   So, the counter is simple, Srinivas said, adding there is an urgent need to pause, verify on a channel one chooses, hang up, and call the person back on the number saved in the phone. Agree on a family code word that only your household knows, because AI can copy a voice, but it cannot copy a secret, he added. Srinivas further said that maintaining digital hygiene is the need of the hour for people around the globe to save themselves from emerging cyber frauds. "People should turn on two-factor authentication for email, banking and social media, and use a different password for each. They must set a daily limit on UPI and card transactions so a single mistake cannot empty their accounts,'' he added. Reaffirming its commitment to safeguarding the hard-earned money and personal information of customers, PNB's Chandra said awareness and vigilance remain the strongest partners in preventing cyber frauds. ''Cybersecurity is a shared responsibility. Your awareness combined with our security measures creates the strongest defence against cyber frauds,'' he added.

item.title: Stellantis India aims to halve vehicle development time, boost localisation
item.description: Stellantis India has a long-standing partnership with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle for manufacturing through a joint venture ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Auto / Stellantis India aims to halve vehicle development time, boost localisation

Stellantis India aims to halve vehicle development time, boost localisation Stellantis India has a long-standing partnership with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle for manufacturing through a joint venture

Stellantis has one of its software and technology centre in Bengaluru (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 20 2026 | 3:59 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Stellantis India is targeting to halve vehicle development time and ramp up localisation for certain models as it prepares to launch 12 products across Citroen and Jeep brands under its FaSTLAne 2030 roadmap, MD and CEO Shailesh Hazela said. "Globally, we announced that our ambition is to cut down our development time for bringing new products from 48 months to close to two years, which is around 24 months. That is what we are working on (for) our products, which we are going to launch," Hazela told PTI in an interview. Stellantis has one of its software and technology centre in Bengaluru.   "[Our] India engineering centre is part of the four large tech centres in the world. We have the largest tech centre and they develop cars not only for Jeep and Citroen, but for models globally. So they have the same mandate [cut in product development time] which they will be following," he said. Also, Stellantis India has a long-standing partnership with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle for manufacturing through a joint venture. Recently, they signed a definitive agreement to expand the scope of their partnership into advanced technology and product collaboration. Also Read

India's auto tech funding at $1.3 bn in 2026, unlikely to match 2025 levels premium

Auto tech cos raise $1.3 bn across 97 funding rounds in 2026 so far: Tracxn

BS-VII clock starts ticking as Centre sets 2029 target for emission norms

European carmakers to favour India as it emerges as global hub: Goyal

Audi India mulls local EV production, aims to double mkt share in 3-5 years

Both the companies plan to jointly develop vehicles for more than 50 global markets and manufacture them in India at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited, the 50:50 joint venture between Tata Motors and Stellantis. On localisation, Hazela said Citroen has localisation level in the range of 90-95 per cent, while Jeep brand's localisation stands at around 70-75 per cent. "We are working on a foundation which is local engineering and local supply chain to get localisation of 90 per cent plus in our products here. That gives us flexibility to be in the pricing range that the market expects," he said. Meanwhile, Stellantis India has announced an investment of Rs 4,000 crore over the next three years as it prepares to launch 12 models, including seven new, across Citroen and Jeep brands. The investment will be mainly in products, localisation for customer experience. Jeep brand currently has four models in India - Compass, Wrangler, Meridian and Grand Cherokee, while Citroen also has four models -- C3, BasaltX, AircrossX, C5 Aircross. Of the new products planned, Jeep brand will get four new models -- one SUV each in B, C and D segments, along with a D segment pickup. Citroen will get three new models -- one C segment SUV, D segment MPV and one A segment car.
